w01q1.intro: Every one of these ten skies changes its mind. The first weather word you hear is true — but it is true about this morning. The answers stay asleep until the clip finishes.

items.say: It was lovely and sunny this morning, but look outside now — it's raining again.
items.teach: Sunny was true three hours ago. The sentence turned around at “but look outside now”.

items.say: It was really windy at breakfast. It's calm now, and the sun is out.
items.teach: Windy came first, so it is the trap. “Now” tells you which half of the sentence to keep.

items.say: It snowed all night, but this afternoon it's warm and the snow is melting.
items.prompt: What's the weather like this afternoon?
items.teach: The snow is in the past — “it snowed”. The question asks about this afternoon.

items.say: This morning it was cloudy, so I took my umbrella. Now the sky is blue and I don't need it.
items.teach: The umbrella belongs to the cloudy half. Wait for “now”.

items.say: It's foggy this morning. Yesterday it was beautiful and hot.
items.prompt: What's the weather like this morning?
items.teach: This one flips the other way — the “now” half comes first. Waiting still works; guessing does not.

items.say: We wanted to go to the beach, but it's too cold today. It was warm all last week.
items.teach: “Last week” is the past. “Today” is the question.

items.say: It was dry when we left the house, but now it's pouring and we're all wet.
items.teach: “Pouring” means raining hard. The clue that they are wet comes after the turn.

items.say: It's not raining now, but it was earlier, so the road is still wet.
items.teach: The wet road is left over from earlier. “Not raining now” is stated outright.

items.say: The forecast said sunshine, but it's been grey since we woke up.
items.teach: What somebody said the weather would be is not what the weather is.

items.say: It was snowing when I got on the bus. By the time I got off, it had stopped and the sun was shining.
items.prompt: What was the weather like at the end of the journey?
items.teach: Two moments, both in the past. The question asks about the second one — the end.

w01q2.intro: Unit 7's own listening words: weather, cloudy, sunny, windy, snowy, rainy.

items.prompt: It's cold and you can see your breath. Which one?
The leaves are falling. Which season?

items.teach: Simple present with It takes an s: it snows, it rains, it blows.

items.prompt: Which word is NOT a weather word?

w01q3.intro: Simple present with It — including the negative, exactly as Unit 7 teaches it: “It doesn't snow in the summer.”

items.prompt: ______ it rain a lot in April?

items.teach: Happening right now takes is + …ing. This is the pattern Week 2 lives in.
Every winter means it happens again and again — simple present.

items.answer: It doesn't rain in the desert

items.prompt: It was sunny this morning, but now it ______.
items.teach: The whole week in one sentence: was for this morning, is …ing for now.
